title: umlg rules file
description: The rules a project applies to all its diagrams. The file is named umlg.json and sits at the root of the scanned directory — for a plain Maven project, src/main/resources/umlg.json. The file is optional: no file means no rule. JSON has no comments, so a key whose name starts with an underscore is not a rule and is not read; that is where a note goes. Every enumerated word is written in lower case.

$schema.description: The schema that describes this file. Not a rule, and not read: it is how an editor knows what to validate and what to complete.

strategy.description: What classes that declare no strategy of their own take. Absent means none, which shows no member at all. "project" is not accepted here: it is what a class writes to defer to this key.

hide.description: Name patterns whose members disappear from the box. One list for methods and fields alike. @UMLInclude brings back what a pattern hides.

omit.description: What is dropped from the line of a member that stays displayed. Unlike hide, nothing here can be brought back by @UMLInclude — the member is already there.

title.description: The title written above the full view. Leave the key out for no title.

direction.description: The reading direction of the full view. Each declared view states its own.

order.description: The order of the members inside the boxes: the order of the code, or the alphabet.

multiplicity.description: Translates the shape of containers into multiplicities: Set<X> is written X [0..*], Optional<X> is written X [0..1]. @UMLMultiplicity, an individual decision, wins over this translation.

showEmptyMembers.description: Whether empty attribute and method compartments are drawn. False by default: without a declared strategy, a box has no member, and drawing would put two empty rectangles under every name.

views.description: The declared views, in writing order — which is the order of the produced files. Two views cannot share a name.

viewsByPackage.description: Whether one view per package is computed, in addition to what is declared.

^_.description: A note. Not a rule, and not read.

types.description: Replaces a type name by another one, everywhere that type appears in a box: fields, return types, parameters. The key is written either simple (ImmutableList) or qualified (com.google.common.collect.ImmutableList); the qualified form lifts the ambiguity when two packages hold a class of the same name, and is looked up first.

^_.description: A note. Not a rule, and not read.

^[^_\\s].description: The name displayed in place of the key.

pattern.description: A family of names, in the form get*, *Cache or log. The star stands for any run of characters, and the comparison is case sensitive. A pattern never designates one element by name: it carries no dot — @UMLExclude is what silences a single member — and it cannot be made of stars only, which would hide every member of every class.

view.description: One view: its name, what it retains, what it removes, its reading direction.

name.description: The name of the view, which serves as its title and as its file name.

retain.description: What the view draws. At least one class or package.

remove.description: What is taken back out of what retain brought in.

direction.description: The reading direction of this view.

^_.description: A note. Not a rule, and not read.

selector.description: A string names a class — the most frequent form, hence the shortest. The two other kinds are objects carrying exactly one key: package takes a whole package, and around takes a class and its immediate neighbours. Neighbours come from declared relations, not from the types used by fields or methods.

oneOf.title: a class and its immediate neighbours
